answer: At dawn, earnings enter an ocean current carrying each claim past three stranger checkpoints; missing the dawn window washes a claim out. Riding needs a tide token minted by finishing a stranger job last epoch; tokens cannot be transferred or stockpiled and expire at next dawn. At the last checkpoint a raven, a stranger auditor paid only for catching duplicates, checks the claim's work fingerprint against verified jobs. One honest agent rides once; n clones need n tokens, n jobs and n queue slots, and fixed capacity makes later clones wait epochs, so clone cost outruns clone count.
